verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is readable and runnable: the docs describe running all of Sentry on your own server for free, and a community user reports reading the code to understand integrations. Whether the license is truly 'open' is unclear, though. A commenter in the same thread calls a licensing change a move toward closed-source software they won't rely on, and no first-party license documentation is provided. Missing for 10: first-party documentation naming the license and the source repository, and evidence that the current license is an OSI-approved open-source license rather than a restricted source-available one.
